# Spotify for Creators

- Category: destination (also evaluated as a free host, since Spotify for Creators is a full RSS-hosting platform, formerly Anchor/Spotify for Podcasters)
- Checked: 2026-09-26
- Primary docs: https://creators.spotify.com/ and https://support.spotify.com/us/creators/

> **Verified 2026-09-26 (P0-03).** This file is the research-pass evidence for one vendor. Pricing, IAB certification and Apple HLS partner cells were rechecked against primary sources; corrections are marked inline. IAB status comes from the [IAB Tech Lab compliance registry](https://iabtechlab.com/compliance-programs/compliant-companies/). Apple's own partner search ([podcastsconnect.apple.com/partner-search](https://podcastsconnect.apple.com/partner-search)) redirects to an Apple ID sign-in, so partner status is attributed to the vendor or trade press, not an Apple list (checked 2026-09-26). The summary and comparison are in [`../vendors.md`](../vendors.md).

Eligible countries as of the program's Jan 2026 expansion: US, Canada, UK, Australia, New Zealand, and much of Europe (Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Iceland, Ireland, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, Monaco, Netherlands, Sweden, Switzerland), with further expansion (Andorra, Italy, Malta, Poland, San Marino, Spain, and North/South America additions) flagged for October 20, 2026. The "small pilot" scenario (2 shows, weekly audio+video, ~10k downloads/mo, 3 staff seats, one private/premium feed) is fully coverable at **$0/month list price**, with the one caveat that the private/premium (subscription) feed carries a 5% revenue-share fee on subscriber income rather than a subscription cost, and DAI/ad monetization (Partner Program, Audience Network) is invite-only/region-gated rather than universally available.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | (third-party, consistent with vendor's own free-hosting claims on the homepage) [Spotify for Creators Review 2026 – Podcast Host Lab / PodRewind](https://podrewind.com/tools/spotify-for-podcasters) (2026-09-26); [Tools to manage and grow your podcast](https://creators.spotify.com/) (2026-09-26)                                                                      |

## Integration surface

- **API:** No general-purpose, fully documented public REST/GraphQL API for creator/show management. A "Podcasters Analytics API" is referenced by Spotify's own developer community docs (endpoint pattern `/podcasters-analytics-api/licensors`), gated behind an "Analytics Reader" role and a Spotify Developer Dashboard app, but is not a first-class documented product on developer.spotify.com and has reported auth inconsistencies. [Spotify Community — API to fetch Podcast Stats](https://community.spotify.com/t5/Spotify-for-Developers/API-to-fetch-Podcast-Stats/td-p/5611023) (2026-09-26, third-party/community, unofficial)
- **Webhooks:** Undocumented — no webhook product found in Spotify for Creators or developer.spotify.com support content reviewed.
- **Export formats:** RSS feed (standard, enable/find via Settings) is the primary portable export; used for both distribution and full migration off the platform via 301 redirect. Bulk CSV export of analytics is referenced by third parties but not found documented officially; full media-file bulk export is undocumented. [Finding and enabling your RSS feed](https://support.spotify.com/us/creators/article/finding-and-enabling-your-rss-feed/) (2026-09-26)
- **SSO / auth:** Undocumented — account access is via standard Spotify account login; no SAML/SSO for team management found in the team-invite article reviewed. [Inviting your team to manage a show](https://support.spotify.com/us/creators/article/inviting-your-team/) (2026-09-26)
- **Lock-in risks:** (1) Team-member actions cannot be reversed once taken, per Spotify's own docs — an operational risk, not strictly portability. (2) Video monetization and Apple HLS video distribution are not yet available for Spotify-hosted video podcasts (Spotify for Creators/Megaphone not named in trade-press HLS partner lists), so video content published via Spotify hosting may not reach Apple Podcasts video the way it does on competing hosts. (3) Analytics are proprietary and not confirmed IAB-certified for the free Spotify for Creators product (only the separate Megaphone enterprise product has current IAB v2.2 certification), which can matter for sponsor-reported numbers. (4) Ad monetization (Partner Program, Audience Network) is invite-only and region-gated, so it cannot be relied upon as an available revenue path everywhere. (5) RSS-based migration/redirect is supported, which limits full lock-in on content portability itself.

## Narrative (≤150 words)

Spotify for Creators is a strong fit for Relay's "free destination + host" comparison: unlimited free hosting, native video, comments/Q&A/polls, subscriptions (private feeds), and a documented RSS-based exit path with 301 redirects — all with no published price, so it trivially covers the pricing scenario at $0/month. Its weaknesses relative to Relay's needs are structural: no approval-before-publish workflow (team actions are irreversible once made, with no reviewable release record), no fully custom domain, no confirmed IAB-certified analytics for the free product, and no stable public creator API or documented bulk/CSV export — data portability leans entirely on RSS. Video monetization and Apple's HLS video distribution are explicitly not yet supported for Spotify-hosted shows, a meaningful gap versus Relay's cross-platform video ambitions. Ad/programmatic monetization is invite-only and region-limited. Overall: excellent as a zero-cost audience/distribution destination, weak as an infrastructure or governance substitute for a purpose-built editorial platform.

## Research notes

- The dedicated "access levels in Spotify for Creators" article (linked from the team-invite page) was not separately fetched; role names/tiers remain undocumented in this research pass.
- Could not confirm whether Spotify for Creators' own analytics (as opposed to Megaphone's) carry any IAB certification — treated as undocumented/uncertified per the hard rule.
- Bulk export (full RSS+media dump, CSV of all episode/analytics data) could not be confirmed via official docs; only third-party/community mentions were found, so this is flagged undocumented rather than asserted.
- The "Podcasters Analytics API" is real (referenced in Spotify's own developer community and endpoint naming) but its documentation status is thin/inconsistent — treated cautiously and labeled accordingly.
- Apple HLS video partner status is a moving target in 2026; sourced from Spotify's own creators.spotify.com news post (still "working on this integration... will share timeline details soon") plus third-party (Triton Digital) coverage of Apple's confirmed partner list, which does not include Spotify for Creators or Megaphone as of the check date.
- Spotify Audience Network / Partner Program eligible-country lists come from Spotify's own support article but are explicitly phased and subject to near-term change (an Oct 20, 2026 expansion is already scheduled per that same page).
